texts.preamble: Da vs Neeraj Kumar Nayak & Others on 7 May, 2019 In The Court Of Ms. Gurmohina Kaur, Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate - 01 Patiala House Courts, New Delhi Cc No. 43994/16 Date of Institution : 16.08.2010 Date of reserving judgement : 05.03.2019 Date of pronouncement : 07.05.2019 In re: Delhi Administration / Food Inspector Department of Pfa, Govt. of Nct of Delhi A-20, Lawrence Road Industrial Area, Delhi-110035 ... texts.facts: The present is a complaint filed under section 16 of the Da vs Neeraj Kumar Nayak & others Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 ( Pfa Act), wherein it is alleged that the accused had sold misb randed food in violation of Section 2(ix)(g)(k) of PFA Act read with Rule 24, Rule 36 (2)(a) and Rule 37 r/w Rule 32(7) and (i) of PFA Rules, 1955. 2. As per the complaint, on 21.07.2009 at about 9:01 pm , the food officials including Food Inspector (FI) NPS Chaudhary and Field Assistant (FA) Naubat singh under the supervision of Local Health Da vs Neeraj Kumar Nayak & Others on 7 May, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/193241039/ 1 Authority (LHA)/ SDM Sh. Radha Charan reached at the premises of Ms. Spencer's Retail, 15 Pratap Nagar, Mayur Vihar, Phase-1, Delhi - 91. The accused No.1 Neeraj Kumar Nayak was found vending the business of various food articles, including Namkeen which were found stored for sale of human consumption , lying in sealed packets of 400 gms, each bearing identical label declaration. The food officials lifted the sample the said food article consisting of 3 sealed packets of Namkeen ready for sale. It was divided into three parts as per procedure prescribed under the PFS Act and Rules and separately packed and sealed. Necessary documents were prepared at the spot including the vendor's receipt and panchanama. Price of the sample was paid to the vendor. One counterpart of the sample was deposited with the public analyst(PA) and remaining two counterparts were deposited with SDM/LHA. Vide report date 30.07.2009, the PA reported that the article was conforming to the standards, yet the sample was found misbranded being in violation of Rule 24 as best before was declared in a misleadng manner and there was also violation of Rule 32 (2)(a). Based on the report of PA, investigation was carried out by the Food Inspector as per the instructions of the SDM/LHA. It was found that Accused No. DA vs Neeraj Kumar Nayak & others 1 Neeraj Kumar Nayak was the vendor of Ms. Spencer's Retail Ltd., 15 Pratap Nagar, Mayur Vihar, Phase-1, Delhi - 91 at the time of taking the sample. Accuse No. 2 M/s Spencer's Retail Ltd. was a company and had appointed Accused No. 1 Neeraj Kumar Nayak as nominee under the provisions of PFA Act/Rules for said Accused No. 2 company and being a company, Accused No. 2 was also liable. It is further averred in the complaint that the sampled article of food "Namkeen" was manufactured by M/s Brij Nandan Enterprises and supplied to M/s Spencer's Retail Ltd., accused No.2. M/s Brij Nandan Enterprises is a proprietorship concern and Accused No.3 Brij Nandan Singh was the proprietor and he looked after its business and such he was incharge of and responsible for day to day conduct of its business. After obtaining due sanction of the Director, PFA, the present complaint Ex.PW1/E came to be filed against the accused for violation of the section 2(ix)(g)(k) read with Rule 24, Rule 36(2)(a) and Rule 37 r/w Rule 32 (f) & (i) of PFA Rules 1955 as punishable under section 7/16(1)(a) of PFA Act for selling misbranded food. 3. Since the complaint was filed by a public servant in writing, recording of pre-summoning evidence was dispensed with and the accused was summoned vide order dated 16.08.2010. Vide Order dated 31.07.2013, the Ld. Predecessor observed that the warranty as envisaged u/s 19(2) of PFA Act, 1954 could not extend to Accused No.1 and No. 2 at that stage and would be considered after the evidence of the parties. Based on the report of PA, notice of accusation u/s 251 Cr.PC was framed vide order DA vs Neeraj Kumar Nayak & others dated 30.10.2013 against the accused persons for commission of offence under Section 7/16 (1)(a) of PFA Act for violation of provisions of Section 2 (ix)(g)(k) of PFA Act,1954 along with Rule 24, Rule 36(2)(a) and Rule 37 r/w Rule 32(f) and (i) of PFA Rules, 1955. 4. At the trial, the prosecution examined two witnesses in support of its case, PW-1 FI Sh Hukum Singh and PW-2 FI VPS Chaudhary was part of the team that had visited the premises of accused and lifted the sample of Namkeen lying in sealed packets of 400 gms each. PW3 is Sh. Hukum Singh who is also examined as PW1 in the present case. These witnesses deposed about the sample proceedings conducted by them on 21.07.2009 and narrated the steps undertaken by them, including disclosing their identity, lifting 3 sealed packets of 400 gms each, dividing the same in three counterparts by considering one sealed packets as one counterpart and separately packing Da vs Neeraj Kumar Nayak & Others on 7 May, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/193241039/ 2 them. A sum of 180/- was paid to the vendor as price of the sample vide vendor's receipt Ex. PW2/A. Notice in form-VI Ex PW2/ B and Panchanama Ex. PW2/C were prepared on the spot. One counterpart was deposited with the PA vide receipt Ex.PW2/D and remaining two counterparts were deposited with SDM/LHA vide receipt Ex.PW2/E on the next working day. PA report Ex. PW2/F was received opining the sample to be misbranded. Further investigation was carried out during which letters Ex.PW-2/G and Ex.PW2/H was written to M/s Spencer's Retail Ltd. regarding constitution of M/s Spencer's Retail Ltd. Letter sent to Brijnandan Enterprises, Plot No. 363, Noida and reply Ex.PW1/C was received. Thereafter, investigation was marked to PW1. Letter DA vs Neeraj Kumar Nayak & others sent by PW1 to M/s Spencer's Retail Ltd. were Ex.PW1/A and Ex.PW1/A1. The reply received was Ex.PW1/B. The reply of accused Brijnandan Singh was Ex.PW1/C. It was found that accused Neeraj Kumar (vendor) was Nominee of accused M/s Spencer's Retail Ltd. and the sample commodity was manufactured and supplied by M/s. Brij Nandan Enterprises to accused M/s Spencer's Retail Ltd. Accused Brij Nandan was found to be the sole proprietor of M/s. Brij Nandan Enterprises and therefore, they were all liable. The consent for prosecution was obtained Ex.PW1/D from Director, PFA. After which complaint Ex.PW1/E was filed before this Court and intimation letter Ex.PW1/F alongwith postal receipts Ex.PW1/G was sent to the accused persons. These witnesses were cross-examined by Ld. Counsels for accused persons. 5. PW1 admitted during his cross examination by Ld. Counsels for Accused No. 1 and Accused No. 2 that as per letter Ex PW1/C, accused No 3 had admitted the supply of sample commodity to accused No.2. The bill of purchase was Ex. PW1/DX. On being cross-examined by Ld. LAC for accused No.3, he admitted that he had not lifted the sample. PW2 stated during his cross examination by Ld. Counsel for Accused No. 1 and Accused No. 2 that he had reproduced the label of the sample commodity on Form VI and admitted that in Form VI it was mentioned 'Gujarat Ka Special Namkeen'. He further admitted that date of packing and the batch number of sample commodity was mentioned in Form VI. He also added that the accused/vendor issued the receipt of purchasing of sample commodity ExPW2/1 but however admitted that the contents of the bill were not legible due to being DA vs Neeraj Kumar Nayak & others faded with passage of time. PW2 during his cross examination by Ld. LAC for accused No.3 admitted that accused No. 3 was not present at the spot. 6. Statement of the accused persons were recorded under section 313 Cr.PC on 13.02.2018 wherein they denied the allegations and pleaded innocence. Accused No. 1 and 2 opted to lead Defence evidence. 7. Accused No.1 Neeraj Kumar Nayak examined himself as DW1 and stated that he was working as Store Manager with Accused No. 2 M/s Spencer's Retail at the time of sampling and the sample commodity was supplied by Accused No.3 to accused No.2 vide bill Ex.PW1/DX. He stated during cross examination by Ld. LAC of Accused No.3 that he had checked the bills which was related to the sample commodity that was taken by the Food Inspector. Accused No.3 Brij Nandan also examined himself as DW2. He admitted during his deposition that he had supplied goods to accused No.2 vide bill Ex PW1/DX and stated that he did not receive any intimation letter through the court and also stated that he did not sell 'Gujarat ka Special Namkeen' to accused No.2. During his cross examination by Ld. Counsel for Accused No.1 and Accused No. 2, he admitted that he had issued the bill Ex.PW1/DX to accused No.2 and he further admitted that at Serial No.2 (1151756) Gujarati Da vs Neeraj Kumar Nayak & Others on 7 May, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/193241039/ 3 Namkeen was mentioned in the bill. He further admitted that Sl. No. 8 and 9 also mentioned about the Namkeen. He further admitted during his cross examination that he had also admitted through his statements ExPW1/C that he had supplied Namkeen to M/s Spencer Retail Ltd. and added DA vs Neeraj Kumar Nayak & others that he had given his statement to Food Inspector.
texts.arguments: 8. It is in these circumstances, Ld. SPP for the complainant has argued that the complainant has been able to prove its case against the accused beyond reasonable doubt, as both the witnesses have supported its case and there is no contradiction in their testimony. It is submitted that the accused persons have failed to rebut the findings as given in the PA Report. 9. On the other hand, Ld. Defence Counsel for the accused No.1 and 2 have argued that accused No. 1 and 2 were only the vendors and the accused No.3 had manufactured and supplied the same and the bill was a part of record. 10. Per contra, it was argued by Ld. LAC for accused No.3 that the complaint was filed after the expiry of shelf life, the right to send the second sample became frustrated. He also argued that as per the Report of the Food Analyst, the sample lifted was 'Gujarat ka Special Namkeen' and the PA report was of 'Brij Namkeen" which was not the lifted sample items. He further argued that no intimation or any notice was given to accused No.3 about the Public Analyst report as per the scheme of PFA Act. 12. In a criminal trial, the burden is on the complainant / DA vs Neeraj Kumar Nayak & others prosecution to establish its case against the accused beyond reasonable doubt. This burden cannot be shifted to the accused and has to be necessarily discharged by the prosecution itself by leading cogent and trustworthy evidence. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in Shriram Labhaya v. MCD [1948-1997 FAC (SC) 483] has categorically held that testimony of the Food Inspector alone, if believed, is sufficient to convict the accused and there is no requirement of independent corroboration by public persons unless the testimony suffers from fatal inconsistencies.
